team.name: MVM-Placement
team.brief: Move the weight matrix-vector multiplies (q, k, v, o, gate, up, down projections) and the embedding, LM-head and sampling ops between CPU-side and PIM placements, favouring PIM for the large per-layer MVMs that dominate LLM time while keeping feasibility.

team.name: Attention-KV
team.brief: Choose where q.K^T, p.V and KV appends run (xbar vs vfu), where softmax runs (star vs elsewhere), KV precision, and the size and bandwidth of the vector-unit memory, star units and crossbar scale, changing them together so the attention path gets faster without exceeding area or feasibility limits.

team.name: Elementwise-Hardware
team.brief: Move the RMSNorm, RoPE, activation and residual ops to the most efficient side, then trade crossbar tile, ADC, cell-bit and transpose-technology choices against area and effort, and set the CPU-coprocessor link to the cheapest coupling that still gives a gain.

move.why: All 252 per-layer weight MVMs are already on xbar, so the largest remaining CPU-side matrix op is the vocabulary projection; moving lm_head to xbar targets the biggest leftover MVM and is the most informative next evaluation.

Crossbar placement already worked for lm_head, and q.K^T/p.V are matrix-vector products that fit crossbar arrays well, so moving attention to xbar while softmax goes to star (with 4 star units to avoid a nonlinear-unit bottleneck) should cut the attention path the most.

Moving the RMSNorm, QK-norm, RoPE, activation and residual ops off the CPU onto the star unit is the most likely big win, since these elementwise ops currently run on the slow host side for all 36 layers and the final norm.

Halving KV precision to 8 bits halves the KV bytes moved and stored on every layer's attention path, and star_units 16 speeds up the softmax that remains on the star unit, so both attention-path costs drop together while the xbar placement stays as it is.

xbar_transpose makes the per-token K append a single row write instead of a column rewrite, which should shorten KV-cache updates in the attention path; the +15% area is the price, and it is a 3-month effort that I would only take if the link move alone does not reach the target.

The elementwise ops are already on star, which the Elementwise-Hardware proposal showed is the most efficient side, so I leave them unchanged. Upgrading the CPU-coprocessor link from cxl to package is the cheapest coupling step that should cut host-transfer latency for both LLM decode and tool-drive

xbar_transpose makes the per-token K append a single row write instead of a column rewrite, which should shorten KV-cache updates in the attention path; the +15% area is the price, and it is a 3-month effort that I would only take if the link move alone does not reach the target.

The k and v projections are the smallest weight MVMs in each layer (grouped-query attention has few KV heads), so they underfill crossbar tiles; moving only them to the CPU may free crossbar time for the large MVMs without touching the embed/sample placements that the verifier has already rejected.

The vocabulary projection (lm_head) is a single very large MVM with a tall output, so it may tile poorly on the crossbar; testing it alone on the CPU isolates its cost while leaving the per-layer MVMs on PIM.

Moving q.K^T, p.V and KV appends from the crossbar to the vector unit, with a mid-size KV memory and higher bandwidth, and shrinking the crossbar to 1.0x to pay for the extra area, tests a different attention path than the rejected xbar-only moves.
